claims.explanation: Lofexidine is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist, and its selective antiproliferative pattern is best explained by dependence on adrenergic/noradrenergic signaling and downstream MAPK/PI3K growth pathways rather than by a single lineage. Sensitive lines are enriched for activating mutations in RTK-RAS-MAPK and PI3K pathway genes (KRAS, NRAS, EGFR, BRAF, PIK3CA, PTEN, NF1), suggesting that cells with high basal or ligand-driven adrenergic signaling and intact downstream proliferative signaling are more vulnerable to alpha-2-mediated cAMP inhibition and growth suppression. Lines with loss of FBXW7, CDKN2A, or other alterations that uncouple proliferation from cAMP/PKA control appear relatively protected.

features.basis: Activating KRAS mutations enriched in sensitive lines (KPNSI9S, CL11, GSU, T3M4, KYSE510); MAPK-driven proliferation may depend on adrenergic/cAMP modulation.
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC95, NCIH1650, HCC4006, KYSE270) are among the most killed; RTK-driven growth may be sensitive to alpha-2/cAMP inhibition.
PTEN loss appears in multiple sensitive lines (HEC265, KALS1, FTC133, ZR751, 786O); PI3K-AKT activation may cooperate with adrenergic signaling dependence.
NF1 loss in sensitive lines (KALS1, S117, FTC133); RAS pathway activation may increase dependence on cAMP-regulated growth.
BRAF-mutant HEC265 is highly sensitive; MAPK activation may sensitize to alpha-2 agonist-mediated cAMP suppression.
PIK3CA mutations in sensitive lines (HGC27, KYSE510); PI3K pathway activation may be required for proliferation that is inhibited by alpha-2 signaling.
NRAS-mutant KU1919 is among the most killed; RAS-MAPK activation may confer dependence on adrenergic/cAMP tone.
FBXW7 mutations appear in several least-affected lines (SNUC5, MKN1, NCIH1648); loss may stabilize oncoproteins that bypass cAMP-mediated growth arrest.
CDKN2A loss in multiple resistant lines (IPC298, K029AX, SNU1214, MHHES1); cell-cycle deregulation may reduce dependence on cAMP/PKA control.
Lofexidine is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist; higher ADRA2A expression would increase drug engagement and downstream cAMP inhibition.
Alpha-2 adrenergic receptor subtype mediating lofexidine effects; expression may determine sensitivity to agonist-induced growth suppression.
Alpha-2 adrenergic receptor subtype; expression could contribute to lofexidine's selective antiproliferative effects.
